name: Le Meridien Saigon
short_description: A riverside Le Meridien on Ton Duc Thang Street in District 1, overlooking the Saigon River near the Ba Son Metro station.
ai_summary: Le Meridien Saigon sits on Ton Duc Thang Street in District 1, directly on the Saigon River and near Exit 1 of the Ba Son Metro station, putting it within easy reach of downtown offices, riverside promenades, and Dong Khoi's shopping and dining. It was the first Le Meridien hotel in Vietnam and carries the brand's arts-and-design positioning within Bonvoy's mid-to-upper tier. Guest reviews consistently single out the river views, spacious comfortable rooms with well-designed bathrooms, and a breakfast buffet with a strong local-and-Western selection, alongside staff who are repeatedly described as attentive to small details like remembering returning guests' preferences. The Club Lounge and a recently refreshed gym also draw specific praise. Recurring watchouts are narrower but worth noting: a handful of reviews describe a subpar or slow check-in experience, some feel parts of the hotel show their age compared to newer District 1 competitors, and at least one review flagged outdated information (an advertised nearby attraction perk that was no longer valid) that guests should double-check on arrival. Overall it suits travelers who prioritize river views and a design-led atmosphere within walking distance of downtown District 1.

faqs.question: Is Le Meridien Saigon on the Saigon River?
faqs.answer: Yes -- it sits directly on the riverbank on Ton Duc Thang Street in District 1, near Exit 1 of the Ba Son Metro station, with river views from many rooms and public areas including the Club Lounge.

faqs.question: How far is Le Meridien Saigon from the airport and downtown District 1?
faqs.answer: It's roughly 8 kilometers from Tan Son Nhat International Airport, about a 20-minute drive depending on traffic, and within easy walking distance of downtown District 1's Dong Khoi shopping and dining strip.

reviews.title: Le Meridien Saigon: Staying in Ho Chi Minh City for the First Time (Full Review)
reviews.author: Eunice
reviews.summary: First-timer's take on a spacious 38sqm river-view room, four dining venues including Chef Sam Aisbett's AKUNA, plus spa, gym and infinity pool, all walkable to Ben Thanh Market and Notre Dame Cathedral.

reviews.title: Hotel Review: Le Meridien Saigon (Studio Suite)
reviews.author: Mark Chua
reviews.summary: Points-stay review of a 55sqm Studio Suite, rating the Level 22 Club Lounge among the best he'd seen; praises the pho-station breakfast but notes dated interiors, motorbike noise and no river view from the suite.

reviews.title: Review: Le Meridien Saigon, Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam
reviews.author: LivingHotel
reviews.summary: Marriott Titanium member scores the hotel 7.5/10 after a points stay with a 22nd-floor river-view upgrade and lounge access; loves the service, gym and beef pho but finds furniture aging and the lounge crowded.

reviews.title: Le Meridien Review: Saigon's Best Hotel
reviews.author: Pierre Blake
reviews.summary: Calls it Ho Chi Minh City's finest hotel, rating it 9.3/10; highlights a corner suite with river views and the 22nd-floor club lounge, described as the biggest he'd seen in the city, plus spa, pool and gym.

reviews.title: Review: Le Meridien Saigon, Ho Chi Minh City Vietnam
reviews.author: James Dozer
reviews.summary: Early review of the then-new 22-story riverfront hotel; praises a spacious Premier Classic room, above-and-beyond service, ninth-floor pool and breakfast, recommending it over the nearby Sheraton for SPG members.
